Em: Every string belongs to this chord, so strum all six with confidence. Stay on your fingertips so the open G string rings.
E: Em plus finger 1 on string 3. Arch finger 1 so it doesn't touch the open B string next to it.
Am: Skip string 6. Keep finger 1 curved so the open high E string rings.
A: Three fingers share fret 2, so angle them slightly; finger 3 can sit a little further from the fret. Keep string 1 ringing.
D: Strum only the top four strings. Aim your strum at string 4 and let strings 5 and 6 stay silent.
G: Stay on the tips of fingers 1 and 2 so strings 4, 3 and 2 ring open; that's where G gets its bright sound.
C: Skip string 6. Finger 2 has to arch over string 3 so the open G rings.
Dm: Strum from string 4. Keep finger 1 on its tip so it touches only string 1.
G_easy: Strum only strings 4 to 1. A stepping stone until the full G feels comfortable.
E7: E major with finger 3 lifted, so string 4 rings open. Strum all six strings.
A7: A major without the middle finger, so string 3 rings open. Skip string 6.
D7: A small upside-down triangle: two fingers on fret 2, one on fret 1. Strum from string 4.
B7: String 2 rings open between fingers 3 and 4, so keep finger 4 curved. Skip string 6.
G7: Like G, but finger 1 drops to fret 1 on string 1. Strum all six strings.
C7: C major plus finger 4 on string 3 at fret 3. Keep string 1 ringing open.
Am7: Am with finger 3 lifted, so the open G string rings. Skip string 6.
Em7: Just one finger: everything except string 5 rings open. Strum all six strings.
Dm7: Finger 1 lies flat across strings 2 and 1 at fret 1. Strum from string 4.
Fmaj7: Keep finger 1 curved so the open high E rings: that open string is what makes it a major 7.
Cmaj7: A C chord with finger 1 lifted off: let the open B string ring. That open string is what makes it a major 7.
Dsus2: D major with finger 2 lifted, so string 1 rings open. Strum from string 4.
Dsus4: D major with finger 4 added on string 1 at fret 3. Rock between D and Dsus4 for a classic folk sound.
Asus2: A major with the string-2 finger lifted, so string 2 rings open. Skip string 6.
Asus4: Finger 3 moves to string 2 at fret 3, one fret higher than in A. Skip string 6.
Cadd9: Fingers 3 and 4 anchor on fret 3 of strings 2 and 1, so changing between G and Cadd9 is smooth.
E5: Strum only the three low strings. Palm-mute near the bridge for a punchy rock sound.
A5: Strum strings 5, 4 and 3 only. Let your fretting fingers lightly touch the higher strings to mute them.
D5: Strum strings 4, 3 and 2 only. Keep the motion short and controlled.
G5: The movable shape with its root under finger 1 on string 6. Let finger 1 lightly mute the strings you don't play.
C5: The G5 shape one string higher; the root is under finger 1 on string 5. Don't hit string 6.
F5: The movable shape at fret 1. Strum only strings 6, 5 and 4.
F: Lay finger 1 flat across all six strings at fret 1, rolled slightly onto its bony side. Pull back with your arm instead of squeezing with your thumb.
Fm: F with finger 2 lifted. The barre now sounds string 3, the minor third, so make sure it presses there cleanly.
F#: The F shape moved up one fret. The note under the barre on string 6 names the chord.
F#m: Fm moved up one fret. Check that the barre presses string 3 cleanly; it carries the minor third.
Gm: The minor E-shape barre at fret 3. Check strings 3, 2 and 1 under the barre one at a time.
A_barre: The E shape at fret 5 is the same chord as open A. Frets this high need less pressure, so it's a good first barre to practise.
Bm: Barre strings 5 to 1 at fret 2 and skip string 6. If the full barre is hard, start by fretting only strings 4 to 1.
Bb: Barre fret 1 across strings 5 to 1, with fingers 2, 3 and 4 lined up on fret 3. Keep string 1 ringing under the barre.
B: Like Bb, one fret higher. Many players flatten finger 3 across strings 4, 3 and 2 instead of using three fingers.
Cm: The minor A-shape barre at fret 3. Finger 2 sits on string 2, one fret behind fingers 3 and 4.
C#m: The Cm shape one fret higher, at fret 4. Skip string 6.
C_barre: The A shape at fret 3: the same chord as open C with a tighter sound. Keep the barre pressing string 1.
